text:
I’ll inspect the repository structure and its primary app, metadata, sitemap/robots, and content surfaces, then report only evidence-backed issues with exact file and line references. The core SEO surfaces are small and already reveal several high-impact conflicts: crawler directives do not match the stated GEO policy, and several routes lack route-level metadata. I’m now checking line-numbered evidence and framework behavior so the findings distinguish definite defects from recommendations. **SEO/GEO audit findings** | Severity | File / line | Problem | Fix | |---|---|---|---| | **High** | `public/robots.txt:5-9` | `Bingbot` and `GPTBot` are blocked, contradicting `geo.config.json:1`, which says AI search crawlers should be allowed. This prevents Bing and ChatGPT search visibility. | Allow search/AI crawlers intentionally; block only training crawlers you explicitly target. Add directives for relevant crawlers such as `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, and `CCBot` if required. | | **Medium** | `public/robots.txt:1-9` | No `Sitemap:` directive. Sitemap discovery depends on external links or search-console submission. | Add `Sitemap: https://atlasroadmaps.example/sitemap.xml`. | | **High** | `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` | Pricing has no route metadata, so it inherits the generic `Atlas` title and root description. It also lacks a canonical URL. | Add a unique title, description, canonical, Open Graph, and Twitter metadata. | | **Medium** | `app/root.tsx:2` | Only a generic title and description are defined globally. There are no `og:*`, Twitter Card, favicon, theme, or default social-image tags. | Add site-wide fallback social metadata and a default share image; override title/description/canonical per route. | | **Medium** | `app/routes/_index.tsx:2`, `app/routes/features.tsx:1`, `app/routes/changelog.tsx:2` | No Open Graph or Twitter metadata exists on the main indexable pages. Social previews and AI citation context are weak. | Add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:type`, `og:image`, and equivalent Twitter tags. | | **High** | `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5-6` | Changelog content is fetched only in `useEffect`, so the initial server-rendered HTML contains an empty list. Many AI crawlers and limited renderers will not see the actual release content. | Load entries in a Remix `loader` and render them server-side; handle fetch failures explicitly. | | **Medium** | `app/routes/_index.tsx:9` | “See all features” is a clickable `
` rather than an anchor. It is not keyboard-accessible and is weaker for semantic link discovery. | Replace it with `See all features`. | | **Medium** | `app/root.tsx:7` | The primary navigation links only to Pricing and Changelog; the homepage and Features page are not represented in normal navigation. | Add crawlable `` links to `/` and `/features`. | | **High** | `app/routes/_index.tsx:5-8`, `app/routes/features.tsx:2`, `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` | Page content is extremely thin and generic. It does not answer specific product, audience, use-case, comparison, or pricing questions that search engines and AI systems can cite. | Add concrete, independently useful sections: target users, workflows, integrations, differentiators, pricing details, FAQs, examples, and measurable outcomes. | | **High** | `app/routes/_index.tsx:5-8`, `app/routes/features.tsx:2`, `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` | No structured data is present: no `SoftwareApplication`, `Organization`, `Product`, `Offer`, `FAQPage`, or `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD. | Add accurate JSON-LD per page; do not add `FAQPage` markup unless the visible FAQ content exists. | | **Medium** | `app/root.tsx:2-7` | No organization/entity identity is exposed beyond the name “Atlas.” This weakens entity understanding and attribution in AI answers. | Add visible company/about/contact information and `Organization` JSON-LD with stable `sameAs` links. | | **Low** | `public/sitemap.xml:2-7` | Sitemap entries omit `lastmod`, and the sitemap is manually maintained. This is not invalid, but it reduces freshness signaling for the changelog. | Generate the sitemap from routes/content and include accurate `lastmod` values where available. | | **Medium** | `app/routes/dashboard.tsx:1`, `public/robots.txt:3` | `/dashboard` is blocked in `robots.txt`, so crawlers cannot fetch the page to observe its `noindex` directive. The result is generally exclusion, but the controls are redundant and harder to audit. | Prefer `noindex, nofollow` for private pages while allowing crawling, or keep the robots block and remove the misleading reliance on page-level `noindex`; enforce authentication server-side. | **Highest-priority fixes:** reconcile `robots.txt` with the GEO policy, server-render changelog content, add complete metadata/structured data, and replace the thin marketing copy with detailed answer-oriented content.
